taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.culm_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: "the culms 5-20 cm. high, stiff, firm, smooth, exceeding leaves".

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: culms "5-20 cm. high", "exceeding leaves", so the plant is as tall as its culms.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: culms "5-20 cm. high".

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: "Rootstocks stout, lignescent, creeping": a perennial.

traits.perennation.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: "Rootstocks stout, lignescent, creeping".

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: "Rootstocks stout, lignescent, creeping"; the photos show close turf rather than separate tufts.

traits.clonal.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: "Rootstocks stout, lignescent, creeping".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: "Leaves 4-9 to a fertile culm, the blades 4-10 cm. long".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: blades "1.5-3 mm. wide, flat or channeled at base, attenuate at apex".

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: "spike solitary, androgynous, bractless".

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: spike "narrow, 8-15 mm. long, 6-9 mm. wide".

traits.sexual_system.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: spike "androgynous", "the upper half staminate, the lower with 10-25 perigynia".

traits.flowering_months.note: Spikes in flower and fruit in July and August, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 194485205, 366727583, 306576441, 30777234, 90253154, 384777041, 89024785, 31999712): the sources read give no count or measure.

generator.params.note: Long-stoloned sedge's (carex-inops) values, changed by hand for black alpine sedge: a close turf from creeping rootstocks, short flat blades (Abrams 1923 p. 290: "the blades 4-10 cm. long", 4-9 to a culm) under stiff culms ending in one small, erect, dark spike 1.2 cm long. Not fitted to measurements.

appearance.organs.panicle.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 290, Carex nigricans: "spike solitary, androgynous, bractless, narrow, 8-15 mm. long, 6-9 mm. wide, densely many-flowered"; scales "dark brown tinged with hyaline margins"; perigynia "brownish". Drawn as one dark brown spike with pale-edged scales and no cluster.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, close turf of short green blades with stiff culms, each tipped by a single small, near-black spike. Organ cards from long-stolon sedge's (carex-inops), recoloured and resized by hand.

allometry.note: 0.12 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows in subalpine parkland. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
